extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of political philosophy and classical literature
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from Plato's Republic Book IV laying out prescriptive standards for organizing an ideal city: the character, education, property rules, and duties of guardians, and the civic virtues (wisdom, courage, temperance, justice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must guard purity of the race (myth of metals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulers should anxiously guard the purity of the race; observe what elements mingle in offspring and reassign ranks when there are mixtures of metals (gold/silver/brass/iron) in lineage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Socrates proposes a founding myth (gold, silver, brass, iron in souls) to justify natural class assignments and to make citizens accept demotion or elevation according to nature; the rulers must not be pitiful when a child must descend in rank, nor fail to elevate superior offspring from lower classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instill and propagate the founding myth across generations
rubrics_metrics.description: The population need not believe the myth in the present generation, but their sons and subsequent posterity should be made to believe it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fostering of such a belief will make citizens care for the city and for one another; the myth serves a civic function to stabilize social roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should establish defensible encampments and perform proper religious rites
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must select a spot to suppress insurrection and to defend against external enemies, encamp there, offer sacrifices to appropriate gods, and prepare dwellings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical military and religious preparation is part of their duty: choose defensible positions, perform rites, and build appropriate dwellings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Houses must suit soldiers, not shop-keepers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians' dwellings must shield them against cold and heat and be suitable to the life of soldiers rather than the private homes of merchants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homes should be functional for guardians' duties; the comparison with shop-keepers highlights simplicity and communal/ martial suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent auxiliaries from becoming tyrannical
rubrics_metrics.description: Take every care that auxiliaries, being stronger than ordinary citizens, do not grow too powerful and become savage tyrants instead of friends and allies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine education, habitations, and institutional checks so their greater strength does not lead to oppression of other citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: True education civilizes and humanizes guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: A really good education will civilize and humanize guardians in their relations to one another and to those they protect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education is the primary safeguard against guardians' moral degeneration; it must be continual and properly formed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Habitations and possessions must not impair virtue or tempt guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Habitations and everything belonging to guardians should be such as will neither impair their virtue nor tempt them to prey upon other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material environment and living arrangements must be arranged to support guardians' temperance and duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must have no private property beyond necessities; communal living
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the guardians should have property beyond what is absolutely necessary; no private houses or closed stores; provisions limited to those of trained warriors; a fixed rate of pay sufficient for yearly expenses only; they will mess and live together like soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents guardians from becoming housekeepers, husbandmen, or tyrants through accumulation of private wealth; common living fosters unity and reduces temptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit guardians from handling gold and silver
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians alone may not touch or handle silver or gold, be under the same roof with them, wear them, or drink from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gold and silver are said to be divine within them; forbidding contact with precious metals prevents corruption and 'pollution' of the divine element in guardians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate social mobility by elevating/demoting offspring by nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Degrade offspring of guardians when inferior and elevate into guardianship offspring of lower classes when naturally superior; assign each individual to the work for which nature intended him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for each person to do one job suited to his nature so the whole city will be 'one and not many'; this institutionalizes meritocratic movement based on natural aptitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve music and gymnastic in original form; forbid musical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and gymnastic must be preserved in their original form without innovation; musical innovations are dangerous to the State and ought to be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damon is cited: changes in musical modes lead to changes in fundamental laws and customs; early training in approved music/gymnastics fixes orderly character in youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early strict training of youth to prevent lawlessness
rubrics_metrics.description: Youth should be trained from the first in a stricter system, because amusements that become lawless lead youths into lawless adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordered play and musical training create habits of order that accompany them throughout life and help maintain civic stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: State size limited by unity; be one and self-sufficing
rubrics_metrics.description: The State should increase only so far as is consistent with unity; it should be accounted neither large nor small, but one and self-sufficing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is the proper limit on territorial expansion; a smaller, well-ordered State of true defenders is preferable to vast but divided polities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against the corrupting effects of wealth and poverty
rubrics_metrics.description: Wealth breeds luxury and indolence and causes deterioration of arts; poverty prevents acquisition of tools and teaching. Both extremes lead to degeneration which guardians must watch against.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain economic conditions for craftsmen and citizens to prevent decline in skill and virtue; guardians should be alert to these social evils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founding aim: greatest happiness of the whole, not of any one class
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in founding the State is the greatest happiness of the whole; guardians should not be given such individual happiness as would make them cease to be guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making one class excessively comfortable (which would corrupt roles); preserve class character so each does its proper function for common good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom: rule by those with knowledge of the whole (guardians)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State is wise by virtue of knowledge that counsels about the whole, not particular crafts; this knowledge resides in the ruling guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guardians are the smallest class but hold the knowledge that gives the city the title 'good in counsel'—true statesmanship requires this presiding knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage as fixed right opinion about dangers (education-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage in the State resides in the part that preserves the opinion implanted by law about what is to be feared and not to be feared; education (music/gymnastics) prepares them to 'take the dye of the laws' so this opinion is indelible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courage is not mere uninstructed bravery; it is the saving power of true, law-conforming opinion resistant to pleasure, pain, desire, or fear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as harmony/self-mastery across classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance is the ordering or controlling of pleasures and desires; it is like harmony or symphony—agreement among superior and inferior about who should rule and the mastery of the better part over the worse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance extends to the whole State (unlike courage and wisdom which reside in parts) and manifests when rulers and subjects agree about rightful rule and self-mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as doing one’s own business (not being a busybody)
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice is the principle that one man should practise one thing only—the work for which his nature is best adapted; justice is doing one's own business and not meddling in others'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By assigning each person to their natural function and preventing role-confusion, justice emerges as the residue virtue once wisdom, courage, and temperance are located in the State.
